**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I am 65 and have farmed this land my whole life. My husband passed, my children are in the city. I manage about 8 mu on my own, though I hire machines for the heavy work now — my back cannot take what it once did. I know two crops: winter wheat and summer maize. That is what my parents grew, what my neighbors grow, what the county extension station helps with. I would not know how to grow anything else or who would buy it.

The wheat goes in October after the maize is off the field. The maize goes in June right after the wheat is cut — sometimes the same week. I rent the rotary tiller and seeder from the village service station, same as always.

For seeds, I buy from the county agro shop in town. They sell the improved wheat variety — Jimai — and a hybrid maize. I do not save my own seed anymore; the hybrid maize cannot be saved anyway, and the shop seed gives better yield. I am not going to experiment with something unfamiliar at my age.

For fertilizer, I use compound fertilizer as base when I plant, then urea when the crop is growing. I do what the other women in the village do. I irrigate the wheat three times — once when I plant to get the seeds started, once at jointing, once at heading. The maize I irrigate once or twice depending on summer rain; this year I will plan for two. I spray pesticides for weeds and for the aphids — twice on wheat, once on maize.
